newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah adjusts to central bank fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah adjusts to central bank fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah adjusted lower against the dollar after the central bank raised its band in the afternoon as expected, dealers said on Friday.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,329/2,521 and the conversion rate to 2,329/2,377.
A foreign bank dealer said operators had widely expected a higher fixing on Friday following a three-point depreciation each in the past two weeks.
Dealers said trading was slow but short-dated swaps were expensive although the rupiah was cheap in the money market.
They said the spot and swap markets were driven by anticipation of the liquidity condition during and after the public offering of PT Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) shares.
BNI is scheduled to begin offering on November 4-7.
One Japanese bank dealer said swap premiums had edged down slightly after rising earlier on offshore covering.
Overnight swap was at 1.2/1.3 and tom/next at 0.55/0.60.
Overnight money was last at around 10.0 percent.
One European bank dealer said some operators seemed to have covered forward positions on expectation of a possible tightening when BNI funds were submitted to the bank.
"There is the scenario that the funds might be placed in central bank papers (SBIs) later which seemed to have caused some adjustment in the forward market," the dealer said.
One-month swap was at 17.0/17.5, two at 34.5/35.5, three at 52.00/52.75 and six at 99.0/100.0 points.
Spot rupiah was at 2,329.0/29.5 at 0920 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,328.5/29.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,328.25/28.90 and 2,327.50/27.75, respectively.
The European bank dealer said sentiment on the rupiah remained bullish and expected it to remain strong in the coming week due to sustained inflows to buy BNI shares.
